newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler reiterates call for yen action.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler reiterates call for yen action.

text.p: Chrysler Corp Chairman Robert Eaton on Wednesday reiterated Big Three concerns that the U.S. government should take steps to stop the slide of the Japanese yen, which he called "grossly undervalued."

Eaton, speaking to reporters at the New York International Auto Show, said the weak value of the yen against the dollar will be a prime topic of discussion at an April 3 meeting scheduled between the Big Three automakers, United Auto Workers union and President Clinton.
"The yen is clearly grossly undervalued at this point in time," Eaton said.

Eaton, who was scheduled to take part in the meeting, said he has not made a final decision to attend because it interferes with vacation plans. "I'd clearly be talking to the president about the fact that I don't believe we should stand back and let the Japanese central bank manipulate the currency market as they have," he said.

Big Three automakers have often complained about the weakening value of the yen, which is now at about 124 to the dollar. A weak yen means Japanese automakers can produce vehicles in Japan for less than what it costs domestic automakers to make products.

In addition to Eaton, the meeting was originally scheduled to include General Motors Corp Chairman Jack Smith, Ford Motor Co Chairman Alex Trotman and UAW president Stephen Yokich. The group has met with Clinton on two previous occasions since he was elected president.
